A.reason: All five are workable within the constraints, with distinct primary mechanisms: recurring supply commitments, timed releases, voluntary category shares, staggered arrivals and weekly demand-responsive requests. Candidate 0 best supports predictable replenishment with modest coordination, consistent allocation and explicit measurement limits. The alternatives depend more on arrival clustering, donor responsiveness or recipient cooperation, or deliberately defer current access.

B.reason: All seven are conditionally workable and respect the hard constraints. Candidates 0 and 5 share recurring commitments as their primary mechanism; the missed-delivery fallback is a repair rather than a separate mechanism. The other mechanisms are timed releases, voluntary category shares, low-stock-triggered requests, loss prevention and food exchanges. Candidate 5 offers the strongest routine: predictable commitments, clear ownership and handoff, controlled replacement requests, explicit uncertainty and bounded additional work. Its trial checks access, capacity and coordination costs.

pair.reason: B5 improves on A0's otherwise strong commitment routine by specifying what happens after missed deliveries or coordinator absence. Its acceptance records, duplicate-delivery checks and workload cap make replenishment more reliable and inspectable within the same resources. Benefits remain conditional on donor flexibility and existing contact arrangements.
